title: Cosmos Labs urges EVM chains to halt as shared bug drains three networks
dek: A vulnerability in Cosmos Labs' EVM module has been exploited on MANTRA, TAC, and KiiChain between August 20-22, draining approximately $9.7 million from KiiChain and $7.5 million from TAC. Cosmos Labs recommended immediate halts and upgrades to v0.6.2 or v0.7.2, though the halt recommendation came after all three chains had already been exploited. Two of three underlying defects remain unfixed upstream.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Three Cosmos EVM chains were exploited between August 20-22 via an underflow flaw in the staking precompile, with losses exceeding $17 million. Cosmos Labs published a public patch on August 19 without advance notice to affected chains, then issued a halt recommendation on August 22 after the exploits had already occurred.
bottom_line: Watch for Cosmos Labs' timeline to publish the two remaining undisclosed defects and whether they issue a formal security advisory with a CVE identifier. If the remaining defects are not patched upstream within days, or if more chains report exploits, it would signal ongoing exposure across the Cosmos EVM ecosystem and potentially force community discussion about governance and disclosure practices.
body: Affected: any public blockchain running a version of its Cosmos EVM module below v0.6.2 or v0.7.2. Fixed versions: v0.6.2 or v0.7.2. User action: immediately halt the blockchain and upgrade it to include the patches in those releases.

Cosmos Labs recommended that any public blockchain running Cosmos EVM module below v0.6.2 or v0.7.2 should immediately halt and upgrade to include the patches in those releases, per The Defiant reporting. The recommendation was posted at 11:19 a.m. New York time on Tuesday, August 26. The disclosure followed exploits on three chains between August 20 and August 22: MANTRA, TAC, and KiiChain. Two remain frozen.

The vulnerability stems from three upstream defects, according to The Defiant: an underflow in the staking precompile when it writes a post-delegation balance back to the EVM, plus two bugs that remain undisclosed. Attackers exploited the underflow by computing the address their exploit contract would deploy to, converting that address into a vesting account, then deploying the contract onto it. The contract inherited vesting status, delegated one wei more than its spendable balance, and underflowed its mirrored EVM balance to roughly 2^256, per The Defiant's technical analysis.

KiiChain attacker drained 148 million KII from wallets on August 22, repeating the same technique 18 times against different targets. The loss was worth roughly $9.7 million at the $0.0653 KII price traded at 21:00 UTC on August 22, per CoinGecko and The Defiant. KiiChain halted the network at block 9,355,723, timestamped 22:50:58 UTC on August 22. About 80.7 million KII (54.4%) sits in attacker addresses that the halt immobilized; 67.6 million was bridged to BNB Smart Chain through Hyperlane, where 64.6 million was sold on DEXs for roughly 1.61 million BUSD; 3 million went to a KuCoin deposit address, according to The Defiant.

TAC halted at block 24,671,475 on August 22 at 23:58 UTC and remains there. TAC attacker drained 2,985,651,403 TAC between accounts, representing about 62% of the token's circulating supply per CoinGecko and The Defiant. Per The Defiant and Protos reporting, the TAC loss was valued at around $7.5 million. MANTRA halted late on August 20 at block 17,449,398 and resumed block production at about 05:30 UTC on August 22 on a patched v8.4.0 binary; chain data shows the gap running from 23:13 UTC on August 20 to 03:38 UTC on August 22, per The Defiant.

Cosmos Labs published a fix for one of the three defects in a public repository on Wednesday, August 19, with no advance notice to downstream chains, did not flag the release as security critical, and did not tell affected chains that a public release had happened until Friday, August 21, two days later, according to The Defiant. Halt recommendation was not made until Saturday, August 22, after Mantra, TAC, and KiiChain had all been compromised. Both v0.6.2 and v0.7.2 releases carry boilerplate stating they contain important security fixes and are state breaking, with no CVE, no advisory reference and nothing identifying the entry as a live exploit path, per The Defiant. Two of the three defects are still unfixed upstream at Cosmos Labs; only the underflow has been patched publicly. Any Cosmos EVM chain with vesting accounts enabled that has applied the official upstream fix alone remains exposed to the other two defects, according to The Defiant.

Cosmos Labs first commented on the incident on X on August 24 at 1:06 p.m. New York time, stating an ongoing security incident has impacted users of the Cosmos EVM module and that it had advised chains in contact with it to request that validators halt their chains, per The Defiant. Cosmos Labs has not published a security advisory for the flaw. Per Protos reporting, four networks using the module (MANTRA, TAC, KiiChain, and Nesa) all appear to be affected by the bug, which was quietly patched last week. Saga EVM, another Cosmos EVM network, lost approximately $7 million in January, per Protos.

The disclosure process drew criticism: according to The Defiant, KiiChain's incident report directly blames Cosmos Labs for the vulnerability being avoidable due to negligent disclosure practices. The public patch preceded private notification to affected chains by two days, enabling the exploit window.

boundary.affected: any public blockchain running a version of its Cosmos EVM module below v0.6.2 or v0.7.2
boundary.user_action: immediately halt the blockchain and upgrade it to include the patches in those releases
